title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry continues to see a mix of funding rounds and partnerships aimed at enhancing satellite capabilities and resilience. Meanwhile, budget discussions are heating up as defense agencies seek to bolster their space initiatives.

themes.title: Funding Flows Steady
themes.body: Katalyst Space's recent $12 million raise for a GEO servicing demo highlights ongoing investor interest in satellite technology. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C underscores the appetite for space startups.

themes.title: Defense Budgets on the Rise
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to space resilience, signaling a commitment to fortifying U.S. capabilities in the sector. This aligns with the growing emphasis on joint force integration and readiness.

themes.title: Partnerships for Progress
themes.body: PiLogic's collaboration with an Air Force lab to develop satellite fault-prediction software exemplifies the trend of public-private partnerships in defense tech. Similarly, Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up to bid on a tactical SDA constellation, reflecting a strategic push for enhanced situational awareness.

themes.title: Geospatial Initiatives Expand
themes.body: The geospatial industry is launching a maritime initiative, indicating a broader focus on integrating satellite data with maritime operations. This move could enhance navigation and surveillance capabilities, particularly in contested waters.
